title: Applications
description: What your services consist of: platforms such as Insights Hub or Industrial Edge, and smaller applications. Each one can have a CIA rating (protection need).
name: Name
ownersHelp: Users and teams who may edit and rate this application: user:<name> or team:<name>
archiveConfirm: Archive {{name}}? It no longer counts for the protection need of its services and disappears from the list and the pickers; its rating, links and history stay.

filters.protectionHint: Applications with this level in at least one dimension

emptyState.title: No applications yet
emptyState.text: Your administrators or designers add the applications your services consist of.
emptyState.textCreate: Add the applications your services consist of, map their Steward platforms and rate their protection need.

services.title: Services
services.empty: No service consists of this application yet. Add it on the service page.

integrations.title: Integrations
integrations.help: Steward platforms that connect to this application. A platform belongs to one application at most. Mapping or removing a platform needs the manage right on it.
integrations.empty: No platform is mapped to this application.
integrations.removeConfirm: Remove the platform {{name}} from this application? The platform itself stays.
integrations.notVisible: A platform you may not see

documents.title: Documentation
documents.help: Living documents that apply to this application. Name the applications on the document page under Applies to.
documents.empty: No document applies to this application yet.

cia.title: CIA rating
cia.help: How much protection the application needs, per dimension, each with a justification.
cia.justificationHelp: Why this level: the damage scenarios that apply
cia.needsReratingHint: The scale changed (was “{{label}}”). It does not count until it is rated again.
cia.mapped: Mapped from “{{label}}” when the scale changed

normal.label: Normal
normal.description: The impact of damage is limited and calculable.

high.label: High
high.description: The impact of damage can be considerable.

very_high.label: Very high
very_high.description: The impact of damage can reach an existentially threatening, catastrophic level.

cia.scaleInvalid: The CIA scale is invalid – protection needs can’t be determined until an administrator saves the scale.

need.title: Protection need
need.help: Per dimension the highest rating of the service’s applications (maximum principle, BSI IT-Grundschutz). Override it with a reason, for example for a cumulation or distribution effect.
need.reasonHelp: Why the derived level does not apply, e.g. a cumulation or distribution effect
need.overrideNeedsRerating: The override needs re-rating after a scale change (was “{{label}}”).
need.noApplications: Add applications to derive the protection need.

serviceApps.title: Applications
serviceApps.removeConfirm: Remove {{name}} from this service? The application itself stays.
serviceApps.empty: No applications yet. Add the applications this service consists of.

scope.title: Applies to
scope.help: The applications this document is about, e.g. an ICAM concept for Insights Hub. Leave it empty when it applies to the whole service.
scope.label: Applications

scale.title: CIA scale
scale.description: The levels of the CIA rating, lowest first. By default the BSI IT-Grundschutz protection needs normal, high and very high.

modes.shared: Own scale for all three dimensions

scale.readOnly: Only administrators can change the scale.
scale.lowestFirst: Lowest first: the order decides the maximum principle.
scale.label: Label
scale.mappingHelp: These levels are no longer on the scale. Map their ratings to a new level, or flag them for re-rating. No rating is deleted.
scale.invalid: Each level needs a key and a label, and every key must be unique (at least two levels).
scale.reorderTitle: Levels change their order or label
scale.reorderHelp: These levels stay, but in another order or with the label another level had: their ratings would mean something else. They are flagged for re-rating.
scale.confirmReorder: Flag the ratings of these levels for re-rating
scale.storedInvalid: The stored scale is not valid (for example from a migration package). The BSI default is in use until an administrator saves a scale.

components.title: Components
components.help: What the application consists of. Processes read them through an input of type application, e.g. all Kafka topics of the application.
components.removeConfirm: Remove the component {{name}} with its tech stack from this application?
components.name: Name
components.nameHint: As processes use it, e.g. the topic name or the image without a tag

stackEditor.help: Products from the endoflife.date list with the version in use. Entries you enter or change here win over an SBOM import.

rollup.title: Tech stack
rollup.help: All components together, coloured by the end of life of each version.

sbom.title: Import an SBOM into {{name}}
sbom.help: CycloneDX or SPDX in JSON, e.g. from Syft or Trivy. Steward keeps only the products endoflife.date knows (operating systems, runtimes, databases, major frameworks); libraries stay out. Entries entered by hand stay as they are.
sbom.urlHint: https, without redirects; the outbound policy applies
sbom.summary: {{format}} “{{name}}”: {{matched}} of {{total}} entries are products endoflife.date knows.
sbom.summaryNoName: {{format}}: {{matched}} of {{total}} entries are products endoflife.date knows.

cluster.readNow: Read the namespace {{name}} from the cluster now
cluster.noCluster: No cluster chosen: edit the component to read its deployments.
cluster.notRead: Not read from the cluster yet
cluster.noCertManager: No cert-manager in the cluster: certificates are not read
cluster.unmapped: Images without a product (add them under End of life → settings): {{images}}
cluster.platformHint: A platform of kind Kubernetes; Steward reads the namespace every 6 hours
cluster.noPlatforms: No Kubernetes platform you may use

repository.notRead: Not read from the Git platform yet
repository.platformHint: GitHub, GitLab or Forgejo/Gitea; the name is then the repository path (owner/repo, GitLab group/project). Steward reads it every 6 hours
repository.noPlatforms: No GitHub, GitLab or Forgejo platform you may use
repository.alerts: Open security alerts: {{critical}} critical, {{high}} high, {{medium}} medium, {{low}} low
repository.register: Add to the credentials register (you review it first)

topic.platformHint: The cluster of the topic; the name is then the topic name. Steward reads it every 6 hours
topic.noPlatforms: No Kafka platform you may use
topic.peekNote: For troubleshooting only: at most 5 messages of 4 KB, fields that look sensitive are hidden, and every read is recorded in the audit log. Only platform managers can read, and only when the platform allows it (variable peek = on).

aws.platformHint: The name of the component is the value of the application tag (e.g. shop for application=shop): Steward lists the resources with it, their costs and the IAM users that carry it.
aws.noPlatforms: No AWS platform yet – create one under Platforms.
aws.readNow: Read the AWS account of {{name}} now
aws.costs: costs this month so far {{current}} · last month {{last}}
aws.registerKey: Add the access key {{id}} to the credentials register
aws.keyDescription: Access key of the IAM user {{user}} in the AWS account {{account}}

credentials.title: Credentials
credentials.help: Entries of the credentials register that belong to this application or one of its components, and entries that name it under "Used by".
credentials.empty: No credential belongs to this application or names it.

lifecycle.title: End of life of the tech stack
lifecycle.help: Steward reads the release cycles of the products in the tech stacks from endoflife.date once a day. Badges show whether a version is supported (green), ends soon (yellow) or has reached its end of life (red).
lifecycle.noPlatform: No endoflife.date platform is set up. Add one under Platforms with the connector type endoflife.date (no credentials needed); the demo comes with one.
lifecycle.status: {{count}} of {{total}} products have end-of-life data, last read {{when}}.
lifecycle.neverRefreshed: {{count}} products in the tech stacks; no end-of-life data read yet.
lifecycle.errors: Could not be read at the last refresh
lifecycle.platformHint: The endoflife.date platform to read. Empty: the first platform of that type.
lifecycle.warnDays: Warn days before the end of life
lifecycle.warnDaysHint: From then on a version counts as ending.
lifecycle.notifyHint: Once when a component's release cycle starts ending and once when it reaches its end of life (event “Tech stack end of life” in the notification routes).
lifecycle.scorecardHint: Adds the part “Tech stack”: attention for a version past its end of life, pending for one that ends soon.
lifecycle.unknown: No end-of-life data for this version
lifecycle.eolIn: end of life on {{date}}, in {{count}} day
lifecycle.eolIn_other: end of life on {{date}}, in {{count}} days
lifecycle.imageMapHint: For Kubernetes namespaces: one line per image and its endoflife.date product, e.g. "ghcr.io/acme/base-node = nodejs". The version comes from the image tag. They come before the built-in list (postgres, node, nginx, redis …).

environments.title: Environments
environments.label: Environment
environments.help: The environments of your organisation in order, e.g. dev, test, prod or eu-prod, us-prod. Platforms, “runs on” links and components offer them; other values stay possible. Production environments come first in end-of-life messages and on the scorecard.
environments.name: Name
environments.unlisted: In use but not on the list – add them to give them a place in the order:
environments.filter: Show the components of an environment
environments.componentHint: Leave it empty when the component serves all environments (e.g. the repository).

runsOn.title: Runs on
runsOn.help: The servers, VMs, clusters and cloud services the application runs on, per environment. Their tech stack counts for the application.
runsOn.systemHint: Systems are kept under Service management → Systems.
runsOn.removeConfirm: Remove “{{name}}” ({{environment}}) from the application? The system stays.

systems.title: Systems
systems.description: Servers, VMs, clusters, appliances and cloud services that applications run on. The operating system and runtimes are kept once per system.
systems.vendorHint: e.g. AWS, Azure, on-premises, the hoster
systems.ownersHelp: Users and teams who may change this system: user:<name> or team:<name>
systems.platformHint: When the system is also a platform in Steward (e.g. a cluster with an API).
systems.platformHidden: A platform you may not see
systems.platformHiddenHint: It stays unless you choose another one.
systems.noApplications: No application runs on this system yet. Add it on the application under “Runs on”.
systems.emptyText: Add the servers, clusters and cloud services your applications run on.
systems.credentialsHelp: Entries of the credentials register that belong to this system: technical users, keys, certificates.
systems.noCredentials: No credential belongs to this system.

maintenance.title: Maintenance
maintenance.description: Planned work on platforms, systems, applications and services. While a window lasts, affected monitors stay quiet, run messages can be paused and availability objectives send no breach message.
maintenance.noteHelp: What is done and what users notice. Sent with the announcement.
maintenance.monthEndHint: On the 29th to 31st, shorter months use their last day.
maintenance.targetsHelp: Platforms, systems, applications and services. What runs on them is reached too.
maintenance.responsibleHelp: Told with the owners of what it affects.
maintenance.changeRecordHelp: The record that approves the change (optional).
maintenance.quietMonitorsHelp: Affected monitors show “maintenance” and send no alerts. Checks are still recorded.
maintenance.pauseMessagesHelp: Check and run messages of runs on affected platforms go to the app only.
maintenance.emptyText: Plan a window so monitors stay quiet and the owners know in advance.
maintenance.cancelQuestion: Cancel “{{title}}”? All coming occurrences are removed; the owners are not told again.
maintenance.endBeforeStart: The window must end after it starts.
